title: Automated host turnover protocol with throughput slices and rollback playbooks
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an automated host turnover protocol for Dedicated fleets that lets operators schedule and execute node turnover with minimal SLO impact. The protocol must reserve throughput slices, coordinate autoscaler handoff, prewarm KV caches for replacement hosts, and provide a tested rollback playbook.

Scope:
- Turnover orchestration: schedule window, pick victims, provision replacements, and cut traffic in incremental slices.
- Throughput reservations: allocate 'slices' of throughputs to ensure guarantees during handoff.
- Autoscaler integration: temporary scale-up policy and hedging to absorb transient load.
- KV cache warmup: automated preheat of KV cache and model KV to reduce tail latency after switchover.
- Observability & runbook: dashboards for per-host latency/throughput, runbook for manual abort/rollback.

Acceptance criteria:
1) During a staged turnover of up to 10% of fleet capacity, 95th percentile latency regressions must be <5% and error rate <0.5x baseline.
2) Turnover can be scheduled and executed via CLI and Console with a single click.
3) Autoscaler policy switches to a hedging mode during turnover and reverts automatically.
4) KV prewarm reduces cold-KV miss rate on replacement hosts by >80% within the first 5 minutes.
5) Rollback can be executed automatically on threshold breach or manually via runbook and completes within configured time window.

Out of scope: full cross-region global sharding; long-running host retirement (>30 days).
